# Physics-based micromechanical modeling for failure prediction in advanced high-strength steels.

I develop constitutive models from first principles, implement them as **Fortran user-material subroutines**, and validate them against **EBSD, DIC, infrared thermography, and mechanical tests**. My work connects microstructural mechanisms to component-scale behavior for automotive forming, crash, and failure prediction.

FROM THEORY TO PREDICTION

## A complete constitutive-modeling workflow

I work across the full chain—derivation, implementation, experimentation, and validation—so model assumptions remain traceable to engineering decisions.
</div>

<div class="capability-rail">
<div class="capability-step">
<div class="capability-top">
<span class="capability-number">01</span><span class="capability-symbol">∂</span>
</div>
### Constitutive theory
Finite-deformation kinematics, free-energy and dissipation formulations, rate- and temperature-dependent plasticity, and thermodynamically consistent damage.

<div class="capability-tools">Thermodynamics · Crystal plasticity</div>
</div>

<div class="capability-step">
<div class="capability-top">
<span class="capability-number">02</span><span class="capability-symbol">{ }</span>
</div>
### Solver implementation
Custom constitutive physics implemented as Fortran UMAT/VUMAT subroutines inside implicit and explicit commercial finite-element solvers.

<div class="capability-tools">Fortran · Abaqus · LS-DYNA</div>
</div>

<div class="capability-step">
<div class="capability-top">
<span class="capability-number">03</span><span class="capability-symbol">◎</span>
</div>
### Instrumented validation
Test design and bottom-up validation from microstructure and coupon response to component behavior across strain rate and temperature.

<div class="capability-tools">EBSD · DIC · IR · V-bend</div>
</div>

<div class="capability-step">
<div class="capability-top">
<span class="capability-number">04</span><span class="capability-symbol">↗</span>
</div>
### Predictive acceleration
Physics-informed datasets and DeepONet surrogates that predict formability and mechanical response without repeating every full solver run.

<div class="capability-tools">Python · PyTorch · DeepONet</div>
</div>

FEATURED RESEARCH

## Crystal-plasticity damage modeling—from derivation to validation

For HR340 and HR550 steels, I derived a thermodynamically consistent damage formulation, implemented it in a rate-dependent crystal-plasticity framework, and validated stress-strain response, temperature rise, texture evolution, and damage across strain rates.

**Published in:** *International Journal of Plasticity*, 186, 104255 (2025)

[See the research](research.qmd){.btn-link-primary} [Read the paper](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijplas.2025.104255){.btn-link}
</div>
